claude_proposed_widenings.name: multi_mode_ongoing_effect
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Control Water grants the caster a choice among four mechanically distinct ongoing modes at cast time, re-selectable by spending a Magic action on subsequent turns. No existing family models 'choose one of N functionally distinct ongoing modes with per-turn re-selection.' The ongoing_effect family has a single operation field; this spell requires a branching selector with a per-turn activation cost to switch.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Until the spell ends, you control any water inside an area you choose...using one of the following effects. As a Magic action on your later turns, you can repeat the same effect or choose a different one.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation.save_gate
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Whirlpool mode deals 2d8 bludgeoning damage via a Strength saving throw when a creature enters or ends its turn in the whirlpool. This is a save_gate embedded in an ongoing effect (fires on creature's turn, not just on cast). OngoingOperation only has roll_modifier and damage_on_hit — neither represents a recurring save-triggered damage effect.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: When a creature enters the whirlpool for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there, it makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d8 Bludgeoning damage. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation.force_move_aura
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Whirlpool mode pulls creatures 10 ft toward the whirlpool center each turn. This is a recurring area-pull (force_move) embedded in an ongoing effect. force_move exists in v4 but is not exposed in any OngoingOperation surface variant.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Any creature in the water and within 25 feet of the whirlpool is pulled 10 feet toward it.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: alter_terrain
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Flood (raise water level 20 ft, create traveling wave), Part Water (create trench + wall), and Redirect Flow (change water flow direction) are all environmental terrain-manipulation effects. The v4 taxonomy has block_travel and create_object but no atom for altering ambient terrain state (water level, physical barriers created from existing terrain, flow direction). These three modes have no mapping to any existing effect atom.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You cause the water level of all standing water in the area to rise by as much as 20 feet. / You part water in the area and create a trench. / You cause flowing water in the area to move in a direction you choose.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: Resolution.probability_gate
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Flood mode's wave has a 25% chance of capsizing Huge or smaller vehicles. This is a raw probability gate (not a saving throw, not an ability check) — a direct random outcome with no ability-score anchor. The current resolution atoms (attack_roll, save_gate, ability_check) all require a roll against a DC or a roll modifier. A flat probability roll is structurally distinct.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Any Huge or smaller vehicles struck by the wave have a 25% chance of capsizing.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: Resolution.ability_check_escape
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Escaping the Whirlpool requires the creature to spend an action + succeed on a Strength (Athletics) check against the caster's spell save DC. This is an ability_check embedded as an escape condition in an ongoing area effect. The ability_check resolution atom exists in v4 but is not modeled in any surface type as an ongoing escape condition.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: A creature can swim away from the whirlpool only if it first takes an action to pull away and succeeds on a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC.
